decisions.reason: As a flagship product closely tied to the firm's sustainability-oriented reusable-packaging strategy, it is unlikely to be withdrawn so soon absent clear evidence of underperformance.
A multi-model foldable container line with its own page signals commitment and fit with the core transport-packaging business, so a large firm with slack would normally continue backing it.

Although only mentioned rather than heavily featured, the stackable crate fits the established product portfolio and there is no sign of performance falling far enough below aspirations to trigger exit.
The rackable pallet line appears less prominently promoted, but it still matches the firm's core capabilities and customer base, making near-term withdrawal unlikely without clear shortfall.
Its own product page and relevance for industrial logistics suggest the firm sees a defined market niche, so behavioral-theory logic points to retention while results remain uncertain.

This pallet variant leverages existing pallet and engineering capabilities, and a large German manufacturer would usually keep such a recent launch on the market unless early results were clearly disappointing.
